response.sql:
WITH per_order AS (
  SELECT orderslink,
         AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal,
         AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio
  FROM fees
  WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005
    AND orderslink IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY orderslink
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio
  FROM per_order
)
SELECT p.orderslink,
       p.avg_rebtotal,
       p.avg_ratio,
       p.avg_ratio / NULLIF(o.mean_ratio, 0) AS relative_ratio
FROM per_order p
CROSS JOIN overall o
ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST, p.orderslink
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Fee rows with a NULL orderslink are excluded, since they do not belong to any order.
A zero feerate is treated as a missing ratio (NULLIF), so the ratio is NULL rather than a division error; AVG then ignores it.
The relative ratio is NULL when the overall mean of per-order ratios is NULL or zero, so the division is skipped rather than failing.
The SQL targets PostgreSQL, which the BIGSERIAL and DOUBLE PRECISION documentation suggests; NULLS LAST places missing relative ratios at the end.
